verbs.name: edit.auto_zoom
verbs.description: Add subtle PUNCH-IN zooms at the EMPHASIS moments of a clip — the dynamic short-form / talking-head look (the frame pushes in on the loud beats, then settles back). EMPHASIS DETECTION is live, from the clip's perception report: trigger 'energy' (default) finds local maxima of the per-window momentary-loudness envelope (Loudness.windows — the same audio facts edit.duck consumes), mapped to clip-local time, non-maximum-suppressed by strength + a min-spacing, capped at max_zooms (default ≈ one per 8 s, never every beat); trigger 'transcript' uses utterance/sentence START times instead (the transcript word model, segmented at.?! or a pause gap, like transcript.remove_retakes), forward-greedily min-spaced and capped. Each emphasis point lowers to a 'scale' keyframe RAMP 1.0 → 1.0+intensity → 1.0 (an ease-in rise, a hold_ms hold at full zoom, an ease-back fall), COMMITTED through the normal edit.keyframe{param:'scale'} path — the existing centred-zoompan render path (the multi-point generalization of edit.animate). The committed op carries CONCRETE scale keyframes, so replay needs NO perception (the analysis is live, the result is deterministic). SET semantics on the scale track: re-running OVERWRITES a previous auto_zoom; a manual edit.animate Ken Burns on the clip must be cleared first (the core enforces they are mutually exclusive — the keyframe channel is the richer eased form). intensity defaults 0.12 (a 12% push-in) and is clamped to [0, 0.5]; intensity 0 or a clip with no clear emphasis peaks is a clean count:0 no-op (no op appended). No loudness windows / no transcript words → an actionable error. v1 zooms are CENTRED (subject-tracked focal points are a record-integration follow-up). VIDEO-track media clips with audio (energy) or a transcript (transcript) only.

clip.description: Media clip id (a video-track clip; energy needs audio, transcript needs a transcript)

intensity.description: Push-in depth: the punch zooms to 1.0+intensity (0.12 = a subtle 12% push-in, the default). Clamped to [0, 0.5]; 0 = no zoom (clean no-op).

max_zooms.description: Cap on the number of punches (default ≈ one per 8 s of clip, capped at 24). The strongest emphasis beats win. 0 = no zooms.

hold_ms.description: How long each punch holds at full zoom before easing back, ms. Default 500.

trigger.description: Emphasis source: 'energy' (default — loudness peaks) or 'transcript' (sentence/utterance starts).

verbs.result: {clip, zooms:[{at_ms, peak, scale}], intensity, trigger, count, op_ids} — the punches are COMMITTED as scale keyframes via an edit.keyframe op (op_ids); peak is the trigger metric (momentary LUFS for energy, the preceding pause-gap ms for transcript), scale = 1.0+intensity. intensity 0 / no peaks → {count:0, zooms:[], note} with no op appended

verbs.name: edit.add_mask
verbs.description: Add (or clear) a vector/freeform MASK on a BASE-track video clip — a region effect (blur/pixelate/black) scoped to a SHAPE, the region-blur / privacy-redaction primitive (region-scoped cleanup; blur a face/label; censor a password). shape: 'rect' (points = 2 opposite corners [[x0,y0],[x1,y1]]), 'ellipse' (points = [[cx,cy],[rx,ry]] centre + radii), or 'polygon'/freeform (points = the vertices, ≥3, drawn closed). All points are FRACTIONS of frame width/height (0..1). effect: 'blur' (default, gaussian; strength = sigma px, default 15), 'pixelate' (mosaic; strength = block px, default 16), or 'black' (solid censor). feather = soft-edge fraction of frame HEIGHT (0 = hard). invert = scope the effect OUTSIDE the shape. enabled:false (or omitting shape) CLEARS the mask. The renderer bakes a feathered shape alpha (resvg) and alphamerge+overlays the effect inside the region (CPU/software path); animatable later via keyframes/tracking. v1 renders on the BASE (first) video track only — an overlay-track clip is refused (clear error). A core op (replay-safe).

shape.description: Region shape (polygon covers freeform). Required unless enabled:false.

points.description: Normalized points (fractions of frame W/H). rect/ellipse = 2 points; polygon ≥ 3.

feather.description: Soft-edge feather as a fraction of frame height (0 = hard edge; default 0).

invert.description: Scope the effect OUTSIDE the shape instead of inside (default false).

effect.description: What to do in the region (default blur).

strength.description: blur → gaussian sigma px (default 15); pixelate → block px (default 16); black ignores it.

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.name: edit.redact
verbs.description: REDACTION — a TIME-BOUNDED privacy effect: blur / pixelate / black-box a SHAPE region on a BASE-track video clip, active ONLY during `range_ms` (clip-local [start,end] ms; omit = the whole clip). The editor-side complement to capture-time anonymization: redact a password / API key / face / PII that appears mid-edit in ANY footage (screen recordings, imported clips). Shares the mask field + render path with edit.add_mask but is SECURITY-FRAMED: `mode` is blur (default) / pixelate / box (solid black censor), and an unset blur/pixelate strength uses a heavier OVER-BLUR fail-safe (never under-redact). shape: 'rect' (points = [[x0,y0],[x1,y1]]), 'ellipse' ([[cx,cy],[rx,ry]]) or 'polygon' (vertices ≥3); all points are FRACTIONS of frame W/H (0..1). feather = soft-edge fraction of frame height; invert = redact OUTSIDE the shape. enabled:false (or omitting shape) CLEARS. Render: the baked shape alpha gates the effect (alphamerge+overlay) with `enable='between(t,…)'` for the range (CPU/software path). v1: BASE (first) video track only; one region per clip (multi-region + motion-tracked + OCR auto-detect are next). A core op (replay-safe). To make it FOLLOW a moving subject, track with edit.track then keyframe the region (until tracked-redact lands).

shape.description: Region shape (polygon covers freeform). Required unless enabled:false.

points.description: Shape points as FRACTIONS of frame W/H: rect = 2 corners, ellipse = [centre, radii], polygon = vertices (≥3).

mode.description: Redaction effect: blur (default, gaussian) | pixelate (mosaic) | box (solid black censor).

feather.description: Soft-edge fraction of frame height (0 = hard edge).

invert.description: Redact OUTSIDE the shape instead of inside.

strength.description: blur → sigma px (fail-safe default 25); pixelate → block px (default 24); box → ignored.

range_ms.description: Clip-local [start_ms, end_ms] window the redaction is active in. Omit = the whole clip.

boxes.description: ADDITIONAL regions (face blur): blur/pixelate N faces or boxes at once, all sharing this `mode`/`strength`/`feather`/`range_ms`. Each box = {shape, points, track?} (fractions of frame W/H); track is the same [{t_ms,cx,cy}] motion-centre array as the primary region. The primary `shape`/`points` is region 0; `boxes` are the rest.

track.description: MOTION TRACK — the region CENTRE [{t_ms, cx, cy}] (fractions) over time, so the redaction FOLLOWS a moving subject. Feed edit.track's `points`. rect/ellipse shapes only; the shape gives SIZE, the track overrides the centre. The renderer animates the alpha procedurally (geq).

ocr_auto.description: OCR AUTO-DETECT — read the frame at `at_ms`, find on-screen PII (email/key/card/SSN/IP/JWT/AWS-key/secret-keyword) via OCR (RapidOCR) + regex, and redact the UNION region of all matches (fail-safe over-cover). Omits shape/points (computed). Needs the perception sidecar + rapidocr; returns found:0 (no op) when nothing sensitive is detected. The receipt reports CATEGORIES + box only, never the matched text.

faces.description: FACE AUTO-DETECT — detect every face in the frame at `at_ms` (YuNet, bundled) and BLUR them all at once (multi-region). The one-click privacy redaction for people's faces. Omits shape/points (computed → one box per face, margin-expanded). Shares this call's `mode`/`strength`/`feather`/`range_ms`. Needs the perception sidecar (opencv); returns found:0 (no op) when no face is detected at the frame.

track_faces.description: FACE AUTO-DETECT option: true/default tracks detected faces over time; false uses only the static detection frame. `track` remains the motion-track array for already-resolved redaction regions.

at_ms.description: Clip-local frame (ms) to scan for `ocr_auto` / `faces` (default 0). Pick the moment the secret / face is on screen.

pii.description: Restrict `ocr_auto` to these PII categories (default: all).

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.name: edit.track
verbs.description: MOTION TRACKING — track a region across a clip's frames (cv2: CSRT, with a matchTemplate fallback) and return its trajectory plus ready-to-apply pos_x/pos_y (and optional scale) KEYFRAME arrays, so a title / PiP / blur-mask can FOLLOW the moving subject. Seed the tracker with `bbox` [x,y,w,h] OR a `point` [x,y] (all FRACTIONS of the frame, top-left origin). Tracks the clip-local window [start_ms,end_ms] (default the whole clip), sampling every `every_ms` (default 100). This is a MEASUREMENT (non-mutating, like verify.*): the op log stays cv2-free and replay-deterministic. BIND the result: feed keyframes.pos_x / keyframes.pos_y straight into edit.keyframe {param:'pos_x'|'pos_y'} on an overlay clip (position keyframes and masks consume these natively). Needs the perception sidecar (python + cv2); returns a setup hint if absent. Read-only.

clip.description: Media clip id to track in (its source pixels).

bbox.description: Seed box [x,y,w,h] as FRACTIONS of the frame (top-left origin). One of bbox/point is required.

point.description: Seed point [x,y] as fractions; a small box is grown around it. Alternative to bbox.

start_ms.description: Clip-local start of the tracked window (default 0).

end_ms.description: Clip-local end of the tracked window (default = clip duration).

every_ms.description: Sample interval in ms (default 100). The tracker updates every frame; this thins the emitted keyframes.

engine.description: Tracker engine (default auto → CSRT, else template fallback).

track_scale.description: Also emit a `scale` keyframe channel (box size relative to the first sample) for a zoom that follows the subject (default false).

verbs.result: {clip, engine, fps, source:{width,height}, window_ms, sampled, coverage, first, last, keyframes:{pos_x:[{t_ms,value}],pos_y,scale?}, points:[{t_ms,cx,cy,w,h,ok}], apply_hint}

verbs.name: edit.multicam_sync
verbs.description: MULTICAM AUDIO SYNC — align ≥2 clips of the SAME event (interview/podcast/concert shot on several cameras) by cross-correlating their AUDIO energy envelopes. Two cameras hear the same sound at the same wall-clock time, so the lag that best aligns their audio IS the time offset between the clips. Decodes each clip's audio to a 50 Hz RMS envelope, normalized-cross-correlates each against the `reference` (default the first clip) over ±`max_offset_ms` (default 15 s), and returns each clip's `offset_ms` + a confidence `score` (−1..1). MEASUREMENT (non-mutating, like edit.track): to SYNC, place/trim each clip by its offset (the agent applies it). Every clip needs an audio stream. Robust to per-camera gain (mean-subtracted + energy-normalized).

clips.description: ≥2 media clip ids of the same event.

reference.description: The clip all offsets are measured against (default: the first clip).

max_offset_ms.description: Max |offset| to search for (default 15000). Bounds the cross-correlation lag window.

verbs.result: {reference, env_hz, offsets:[{clip, offset_ms, score, reference?}], sync_hint} — offset_ms = how much LATER the clip's audio is than the reference

verbs.name: edit.multicam_switch
verbs.description: AUTO ACTIVE-SPEAKER multicam switching — given ≥2 audio-SYNCED camera angles of one scene (each on its own VIDEO track, already time-aligned on the timeline — run edit.multicam_sync and place the clips first), cut the program to whichever camera is the ACTIVE SPEAKER (loudest) over time: the interview / podcast multicam edit. Per 250 ms window across the angles' OVERLAPPING span, each camera's audio energy is read from its perception Loudness.windows envelope (the same audio facts edit.duck / edit.auto_zoom use), mapped to timeline coordinates; the loudest camera wins, with a small energy HYSTERESIS so two near-equal levels don't flicker. Adjacent same-camera windows merge into shots, and any shot shorter than `min_shot_ms` (default 1500) is dissolved, so there are no sub-second cuts. REPRESENTATION (replay-safe): an ORCHESTRATOR like assemble.broll — records NO op of its own; it wraps the build in an auto-checkpoint, (re)creates a reserved `__mc_program` VIDEO track ON TOP (later video tracks composite over earlier ones, so a full-frame opaque clip occludes the angles beneath → exactly one angle shows), and LOWERS each shot to a plain edit.insert of the active angle's segment at the sync-correct source offset. Existing user tracks named `program` are preserved and not auto-detected as camera angles. AUDIO is unchanged — video tracks contribute no audio to the render (it mixes from audio tracks only), so this switches the PICTURE, not the sound (standard multicam practice; no per-cut audio jumps). One dominant speaker → one shot / no switches (clean, not an error). <2 angles, an angle with no audio energy, or no overlapping span → an actionable error. SPEAKER-IDENTITY MODE (speaker-identity mode): when a diarization exists for the reference/`diarize_asset` (run media.diarize first), pass `mode:"speaker"` (or rely on AUTO) to cut to the camera of whoever is SPEAKING — each diarized speaker is mapped to the angle whose mic is loudest during their turns, so an off-camera loud noise no longer steals the shot; `mode:"energy"` forces the loudest-mic default. LIMITS: 250 ms window granularity; assumes the angles are already time-aligned; speaker→camera correlation needs per-angle mic separation.

tracks.description: The camera-angle VIDEO track ids to switch between (≥2). Omit to auto-detect every video track holding a media clip.

min_shot_ms.description: Minimum shot length, ms — no cut faster than this (the anti-flicker / no-sub-second-cut floor). Default 1500.

reference_track.description: The anchor / default angle the program opens on and falls back to on near-equal levels (must be one of `tracks`). Default: the first angle.

mode.description: SPEAKER-IDENTITY cutting (speaker-identity mode): "speaker" cuts to the camera of whoever is SPEAKING — each diarized speaker is mapped to the angle whose mic is loudest during that speaker's turns, so an off-camera loud noise no longer steals the shot (needs media.diarize on the reference/diarize asset). "energy" is the original loudest-mic behavior. Omit for AUTO: speaker mode when a diarization is available, else energy.

diarize_asset.description: The asset whose diarization (media.diarize speaker_turns) drives speaker mode. Default: the reference angle's asset. Must be one of the camera angles' assets (its track gives the timeline↔source mapping). Ignored in energy mode.

verbs.result: {shots:[{start_ms, end_ms, camera, energy}], switches, tracks, min_shot_ms, program_track, span_ms, mode, checkpoint, revert_hint, note} — the active angle of each shot is COMMITTED as a plain edit.insert onto the reserved `__mc_program` video track (an orchestrator: no op of its own; revert via the checkpoint; replay/diff need no diarization — diarization is read at PLAN time only). `camera` is the on-screen angle's track id, `energy` its mean momentary LUFS over the shot, `switches` = shots−1. `mode` reports {mode:"speaker"|"energy", and in speaker mode diarize_asset, num_speakers, speaker_to_cam:[{speaker, camera}]}
